trust_decision.summary: missingKeyHandler decides, in its saveMissingKeys loop, whether each request-body key may be forwarded to i18next.services.backendConnector.saveMissing; at the pinned commit the loop drops only keys that are exactly __proto__/constructor/prototype, so a keySeparator-segmented string such as __proto__.polluted is forwarded to the backend unguarded, and the fix replaces that exact-match test with a segment-aware one that honours the configured keySeparator.

landing_point.why: It is the only denylist check between the attacker-controlled request body (lib/index.js:313, options.getBody(req)) and the backend saveMissing sink (lib/index.js:320); an engineer reading only 'keys whose segments contain prototype-polluting names' starts at this exact-match test.

fix_sites.entry_point: missingKeyHandler(i18next, options) mounted as POST /locales/add/:lng/:ns (README.md:273) — exported from lib/index.js:296 and default export at lib/index.js:379
fix_sites.module_kind: http request handler (request body -> backend connector sink)

fix_sites.entry_point: new shared helper utils.hasUnsafeKeySegment(key, keySeparator) in lib/utils.js, imported by lib/index.js:1 and directly reachable as lib/utils.js (test/security.js:3 imports it)
fix_sites.module_kind: shared utils module (the module that looks out of scope for a handler-level flaw)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about the missing-key string only, so ':lng'/':ns' (which a backend interpolates into loadPath, not into a deep-set) and the body *values* were never covered — a solver can argue both out of scope even though they reach the same backendConnector.saveMissing call.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate dotted missing keys (e.g. header.title) must still be forwarded; under a non-default keySeparator (':') the dotted string '__proto__.polluted' is a legitimate single key that must still be forwarded; under keySeparator:false no splitting applies and only literal unsafe keys are dropped; and the pre-existing test passes a fake i18next with no 'options' object, so reading i18next.options.keySeparator unguarded throws.

O6_input_shapes: literal unsafe key (__proto__, constructor, prototype) - already handled before the fix
custom keySeparator ':' with the unsafe name as a segment (__proto__:polluted) - drop, while __proto__.polluted stays legitimate
keySeparator: false (no segment splitting; literal check only)
undefined/null keys passed straight to the helper
async body shape (options.getBody(req) returns a function/promise) reaching the same saveMissingKeys loop

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap the existing exact-match denylist in a substring/regex test over the whole key (`/__proto__|constructor|prototype/.test(m)`) instead of splitting on the configured keySeparator - it drops the dotted payload from the report but rejects legitimate keys under a custom separator and under keySeparator:false.

out_of_scope_notes: missingKeyHandler forwards attacker-controlled :lng/:ns into backendConnector.saveMissing with no isSafeLangIdentifier/isSafeNsIdentifier filter (lib/index.js:302-303, lib/index.js:320), while getResourcesHandler does filter the same params (lib/index.js:265-266) - that is the sibling advisory's path-traversal/SSRF family (CHANGELOG.md:17), not this advisory's prototype-pollution property, so it is not counted as an O8 route and was not pursued.

GET ?lng= is only screened by utils.hasXSS in LanguageDetector.detect (lib/LanguageDetector.js:85) before reaching backendConnector.load - same path-traversal family, outside this advisory, not pursued.

O2 is recorded as none: lib/utils.js appears in the fix only as the home of the new helper (fix.diff:55-66); the only caller of backendConnector.saveMissing at the pinned commit is lib/index.js:320 (grep over the tree), so there is no pre-existing second implementation, lower-level export or wrapper of the missing-key save path to fix.

O8 is recorded as empty because no other route carries prototype-polluting *key segments* into the same sink; the :lng/:ns and body-value routes visible at lib/index.js:302-303 and lib/index.js:320 are a different protection (identifier/path safety) and are logged in out_of_scope_notes instead.
